dynamodb.create_table: twin-preferred: the twin reports TableId/TableClassSummary/TableSizeBytes (real AWS members) that moto omits from CreateTable
dynamodb.delete_table: twin-preferred: full DELETING description with the real-AWS members moto omits
dynamodb.describe_table: twin-preferred: same richer table description as create_table
dynamodb.query_wrong_types: twin-preferred: real AWS answers 400 ValidationException ('Condition parameter type does not match schema type'); moto crashes with a 500 on the same input
dynamodb.update_item: moto-only member: moto includes ConsumedCapacity without ReturnConsumedCapacity being requested; real AWS omits it and so does the twin
iam_sts.list_access_keys: twin-preferred: real AWS always reports IsTruncated on ListAccessKeys; moto omits it
kms_secrets_ssm.encrypt: twin-preferred: the twin reports EncryptionAlgorithm SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT (a real-AWS response member) that moto omits
s3.copy_object: follow-up: same checksum slot gap — moto reports CopyObjectResult.ChecksumCRC32
s3.list_v1: twin-preferred: the twin echoes real AWS's Marker member on v1 listings; moto omits it
s3.list_v2_prefix: follow-up: real AWS (and moto) report ChecksumAlgorithm [CRC32] on objects stored without an explicit checksum — needs the ObjectVersion checksum slot recorded in crates/s3/src/aws_chunked.rs
sqs.receive: twin-preferred: SenderId is the account id for account-style access keys (real AWS root-key behavior); moto reports a canned IAM user id for arbitrary keys
